title: Complete reports leave longitudinal measurement reliability unresolved
claim: In BR-037, four Terra/high attempts on three selected I-SPY2 patients completed and passed the mechanical reporting contract. They localized the dominant finding and avoided asserting pathological clearance; two neutral runs declined follow-up diameter measurement. The neutral/cue pair reported about 5.9% versus 27.2% shrinkage using different phases, thresholds, smoothing and box conventions, leaving measurement reliability unresolved.
limitations: Agents received two full reconstructed examinations with neutral sequence/timing metadata; later visits, source measurements, pathology outcomes and diagnosis-bearing private tags were withheld.
Mechanical completion is not a clinical pass. The post-hoc measurement audit reproduces the reported methods without validating them clinically.

One cue pair changes both instructions and analysis choices, so it cannot establish a general prompt effect. Deliberately stratified public cases do not support prevalence or population accuracy estimates.
No Sol comparison or brain-MRI trial was run; BR-018 is a historical scaffold, not a completed experiment. No observed source-case retrieval does not establish absence of pretraining exposure.
Source diameter units remain unresolved; retained source comparisons use unit-invariant percentage changes.
